name: 35mm film photo
means: Colour negative film: highlights that roll off instead of clipping, halation blooming out of bright edges, slightly crossed colour in the shadows, and grain through the midtones.
prose: a 35mm colour negative film photograph, highlights rolling off softly instead of clipping, halation blooming around bright edges, slightly green-shifted shadows against warm midtones, modest contrast, muted natural palette
negative_add: digital clarity, hdr, oversharpened, clipped highlights, illustration, anime
works_for: video only halfway. The colour behaviour survives; the grain does not - fine per-pixel texture baked into a keyframe boils through i2v. If you want grain on a clip, add it to the FINISHED video with an ffmpeg noise filter, where it is temporally random the way real grain is instead of a smeared still. Reasoned from the measured grain result, not measured on video.
note: Half of this style is not deliverable from a prompt at all. studio/tags/film_grain.json is the best-measured failure in the project: four grain settings came back as four unrelated portraits with no visible grain difference, because grain is a per-pixel property and a diffusion sampler has no handle on it - which is exactly why studio/looks/faded_film.json deliberately leaves grain out of its tags rather than promise a texture it cannot deliver. What DOES land on qwen is the colour crossover and the highlight roll-off. Take those from the prompt, take the grain from ffmpeg, take the fade from the faded_film look. Unavailable on the anime checkpoint. | Downgraded to untested: NOTHING in this library was rendered when it was authored, so every strength and engine call is a considered prediction. This project's own standard - written on the Illustrious checkpoint card - is that a recommendation is not a measurement.
verdict: Warmer, softer, slight halation. Subtle but present.
